ideas.name: Anti-Virus Design Software
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Architects and builders would buy it, and any software firm could write the same thing, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Laying out buildings to slow infection is a helpful feature of design software, not a new industry.

ideas.author: John Ringo
ideas.line: A medicine that keeps soldiers alert through long stretches without rest.
ideas.name: Provigil-C
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: The description names soldiers, so the army pays; wakefulness drugs are widely made, so the firms that already supply military medicine collect.
verdict.prize_why: Keeping troops alert through long operations is worth a good deal to any army.

ideas.author: Donald Kingsbury
ideas.line: A wrist device that damps shaking in the hands.
ideas.name: Inertial Bracelet
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Wearers would buy it, and it is a simple device many firms could make, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Steadying shaking hands helps people with a few conditions.

ideas.author: Alastair Reynolds
ideas.judged: AI models' likeliest decade: 2100 or later
ideas.line: A hybrid creature blending pig and human genes.
ideas.name: Hyperpig
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Nothing is sold, so no seller keeps anything.
verdict.prize_why: The description gives the creature no use that a buyer would pay for, unlike made creatures bred for work, organs or company, so there is nothing to price.

ideas.author: John Ringo
ideas.line: A pill that removes fatigue itself rather than merely masking sleepiness.
ideas.name: Provigil
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: People would buy it for themselves, and a medicine that truly did this would be new and protected from copying for a long while, so its maker keeps much of the gain.
verdict.prize_why: Removing fatigue itself, not just masking it, is the promise of doing without sleep and would hand nearly every adult many more waking hours; the real medicine of this name does less.

ideas.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
ideas.line: An implant that stimulates a nerve to stop queasiness without medication.
ideas.name: Vagus Nerve Bio-Chip
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: People would buy it for themselves, and several firms could build such an implant, so established makers of medical devices collect.
verdict.prize_why: Stopping queasiness without medicine is a convenience for travellers and some patients.

ideas.author: Richard Morgan
ideas.line: A robotic machine that performs operations, with doctors on hand.
ideas.name: Autosurgeon
ideas.profit: a moderate profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: I assumed hospitals and clinics buy it; with the needed machine intelligence widely available several firms could build it, so established medical equipment makers and hospital groups collect.
verdict.prize_why: A machine that operates would cut the cost of surgery, but with doctors still on hand it changes only that part of medicine.

ideas.author: Richard Morgan
ideas.line: Old-fashioned lenses worn in front of the eyes to fix poor sight.
ideas.name: External Eyelenses
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: People buy them for themselves, and lenses are simple to grind and sold everywhere, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Correcting poor sight serves a large share of all people, though the story treats it as old-fashioned.

ideas.author: Margaret Atwood
ideas.line: A genetically modified pig raised to supply organs for human transplant.
ideas.name: Pigoon
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Patients pay, with insurers behind them, and since the animals breed, established farms and transplant centres collect.
verdict.prize_why: A steady supply of organs for transplant would be worth an industry.

ideas.author: Richard Morgan
ideas.line: A coating sprayed onto a surgeon's hands to form a thin sterile glove.
ideas.name: Spray-on Surgical Gloves
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Hospitals would buy it, and many makers of medical supplies could mix such a spray, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A sprayed glove is a small saving of time and fuss in the operating room.

ideas.author: Robert J. Sawyer
ideas.line: A light-based treatment that wipes out unwanted biological molecules inside a person.
ideas.name: Tuned-Laser Decontamination
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: I assumed hospitals and border posts buy the equipment; other makers could copy it once it worked, so established medical equipment firms collect.
verdict.prize_why: Clearing germs and other unwanted matter from inside a person with light would replace many medicines and change how infection is treated.

ideas.author: Iain M Banks
ideas.line: An oxygen-rich liquid breathed into the lungs so the body can withstand high pressure.
ideas.name: Gillfluid
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Firms would buy it for their crews, and I assumed the liquid is a chemical many firms could make, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Breathing liquid to bear high pressure serves a few divers and space crews.

ideas.author: John Scalzi
ideas.judged: AI models' likeliest decade: 2100 or later
ideas.line: Engineered human skin that photosynthesises, letting the body draw some energy from sunlight.
ideas.name: KloraDerm
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: I assumed people buy it for themselves from clinics; the method could be copied, so clinics already offering such treatments collect.
verdict.prize_why: The story promises only a little energy from sunlight, which is a curiosity beside ordinary food.

ideas.author: Paul Di Filippo
ideas.judged: AI models could not judge when it may arrive
ideas.line: A single tablet that eliminates the body's requirement for sleep.
ideas.name: A-Som (Antisomnolence Drugs)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: People would buy it for themselves, and a new drug is protected from copying for a long while, so its maker keeps much of the gain.
verdict.prize_why: Doing away with sleep would hand nearly every adult many more waking hours, changing how most people live and work.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.judged: AI models could not judge when it may arrive
ideas.line: A fictional engineered plant used for social control in the story.
ideas.name: Blithe
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Assuming it is outlawed for everyone, governments and employers included, nothing is sold.
verdict.prize_why: It is done to a person without their say, to hurt them, break their mind or override their will or body, which no one may lawfully buy or use.

ideas.author: Robert J. Sawyer
ideas.line: An external processor unit that drives an implant restoring sight.
ideas.name: EyePod
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Patients would pay, mostly through insurers or health services, and once the design was known other device makers could copy it, so established implant makers and eye clinics collect.
verdict.prize_why: Giving sight back to blind people is worth an industry of its own, though most people would never need it.

ideas.author: Alan Dean Foster
ideas.line: A person whose body has been extensively modified with engineered or artificial parts.
ideas.name: Humeld
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Patients would pay, mostly through insurers or health services, and other firms could copy the parts, so established implant makers and the hospitals that fit them collect.
verdict.prize_why: The name is of the person, so the thing judged is the fitting of engineered and artificial parts to the body, which taken together covers replacement eyes, limbs and organs and is an industry of its own.

ideas.author: Alan Dean Foster
ideas.line: An implanted apparatus that takes over and improves how the body processes food.
ideas.name: Nutrient Extractor and Maximizer (NEM)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Patients pay, and makers of medical implants collect since rivals could build the same device.
verdict.prize_why: An implant that improves how the body uses food would be wanted by a great many people.

ideas.author: M.T. Hill
ideas.line: A drug that puts a traveller into a brief hibernation-like torpor for the length of a flight.
ideas.name: Sloth Pill
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Travellers would buy it for themselves, and a new drug is protected from copying for a while, so its maker keeps what is left.
verdict.prize_why: Sleeping through a single flight is a comfort for travellers, unlike the long dormancy that makes far voyages possible.

ideas.author: Nick Harkaway
ideas.line: A moldable tissue substitute pressed into wounds to fill damaged flesh.
ideas.name: Flesh Putty
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Hospitals and clinics would buy it, and the firms that already supply wound dressings could all make it, so they collect a modest margin.
verdict.prize_why: Man-made skin helps people with burns and bad wounds, which is an important but narrow part of medicine.

prizes.means: Meets a basic need for a large share of humanity, or changes how most people live or work.
Worth an industry of its own, or changes what one industry costs to run.
Not something anyone would pay for: a hazard, a custom, or something no one may buy.

rows.means: Anyone can make it, so competition leaves no seller much.
Whoever builds it first can stop others copying it, or controls something others cannot get.
It is easy to copy, and firms that already own what is needed to sell it collect.
Only those a government permits may sell it, and permits are scarce.
